entities.name: Khanegah Mosque (Quba)
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Khanegah Mosque Quba (Persian: مسجد خانقاه قبا) is one of the mosque complexes in the Quba area of Medina, Saudi Arabia — a locality of extraordinary Islamic historical significance as the site of the Masjid Quba (Quba Mosque), the first mosque ever built in Islamic history (622 CE), erected by the Prophet Muhammad upon his arrival from Mecca at the beginning of the Hijra (migration) that marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

Quba's historical significance is immense: it was the location of the Prophet Muhammad's first stop after leaving Mecca during the Hijra (622 CE), and the Quran (9:108) specifically praises the Quba mosque as one 'founded from the first day on piety.' The Prophet reportedly said that praying two rak'ahs (units of prayer) at Quba is equivalent to the reward of one Umrah (minor pilgrimage). The area around Quba thus developed as one of the most religiously significant zones in Medina, with multiple mosque buildings and religious complexes.

A khanegah (خانقاه, also written khanqah or khaneqah) is a Sufi lodge — a building complex used by Sufi orders (tariqas) for communal living, spiritual practice, and teaching. The combination of khanegah (Sufi lodge) and mosque in the sacred Quba area reflects the historical presence of Sufi orders in Medina and their establishment of spiritual centers in the sacred geography of early Islam.
